title: Booleans and empty strings as attribute values, one table (FORMA-182 findings F2 and F3; DR-9 rule 6's attribute half, the attribute table of design 4 rule 5)
contract: An attribute named in `booleanAttributes` (core's HTML boolean set) follows presence: true writes it bare, false and null omit it. Every other attribute (data-*, aria-*, class, title, …) is written as the value's string: true is the word "true", a string is itself, the empty string included (`title=""`), and false and null omit it. The same on every writer: the walker's DYN_ATTR over a slot, the compiler's static attributes, h() static and reactive, and adoption's expectations and later writes. A value the compiler knows at build time to be the empty string is written by the server, not dropped: a client slot cannot hold an empty default (zero default bytes mean no default, which the walker reads as null), so the compiler writes such an attribute as a static `name=""`. Names are matched as written, lower-case.
consumers: crates/forma-ir/src/walker.rs > value_rule_vectors (DYN_ATTR over each `values` slot; the walker's boolean set equals `booleanAttributes`)

packages/compiler/tests/value-rule-6-attributes.test.ts (each `compiled` shape builds without a diagnostic and its attribute reads `dom` under the defaults; the compiler's boolean set equals `booleanAttributes`)

packages/core/src/dom/__tests__/value-rule-6-attributes.test.ts (h() static and reactive, adoption's expectation and later writes, for each `values` entry; core's boolean set equals `booleanAttributes`)
packages/core/e2e/value-rules.spec.ts (each `values` entry served as the walker writes it, parsed by the three engines and strictly adopted without a write, static and reactive)
note: Hand-enumerated. In `values`, `value` is the slot's value (a JSON boolean, string or null), `html` the attribute exactly as the walker writes it after the tag name (empty when it is omitted) and `dom` the attribute's value in the DOM (null when absent). In `compiled`, `tag` defaults to `p`, `setup` is a module-level statement and `value` the attribute's source expression; `dom` is what the attribute reads under the slot defaults. F2: a reactive `true` on a non-boolean attribute was bare from the walker and "true" from core. F3: a client signal defaulting to '' was dropped by the walker where core writes `value=""`.
